articles.title: Andy Burnham says he’s ‘increasingly confident’ early release of PC Harper killers can be prevented - UK politics live
articles.description:
The prime minister says other work to reduce prisoner numbers could allow for more space for serious offenders

Andy Burnham has said that in an ideal world he would not want to see “a single prisoner” released early.

Speaking to reporters on a visit in Derbyshire, he also said that his decision to order the justice secretary to look again for a means of excluding the killers of PC Andrew Harper from the early release scheme coming into force in the autumn was evidence of how he has “never taken no for an answer”.

I don’t want to see a single prisoner released early, and that’s the spirit that I’ve brought to the first three weeks that I’ve served as prime minister, and I’ve always worked like that.

I’ve never taken no for an answer, not in the past dealing with Hillsborough and other issues, and not now when I’m facing the situation that I’m looking at now. It’s always been my style, I won’t give up, and I believe there is more I can do.
